stem: Examine the series: 2, 5, 11, 20, 32, 47, ?. Which value completes it correctly?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Misidentifying the next first-difference as 15 (rather than 18) gives 47 + 15 = 62, treating the first differences as increasing by 3 each time instead of tracing the true second-difference pattern.
Correctly computing the next first-difference as 17 but slipping to add 17 to 47 as 64 instead of 65.
First differences: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. Second differences: all 3. The next first-difference is 18. So the next term is 47 + 18 = 65.
Using a next first-difference of 21 instead of 18 (adding 6 to the last first-difference of 15 instead of 3) gives 47 + 21 = 68.

explanation: First differences of the series: 5-2=3, 11-5=6, 20-11=9, 32-20=12, 47-32=15. These differences 3,6,9,12,15 form an AP with common difference 3. The next first-difference is 15+3=18. The next term is 47+18=65. Hidden trap: the first differences look like multiples of 3 (3,6,9,12,15) which is itself a GP with ratio 2 only for the first few terms - the genuine pattern is a second-order AP with constant second-difference of 3.

explanation_sections.punchline: The first differences 3,6,9,12,15 are themselves an AP (d=3), but candidates may confuse this with a GP (ratio 2) for the first few terms - the second-difference test settles it unambiguously.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: compute first differences 3,6,9,12,15; then second differences 3,3,3,3 (constant at 3). Next first-difference = 15+3 = 18. Next term = 47+18 = 65. Verify: second-difference model predicts T(n) = n^3/2 ... confirm by the quadratic fit.
explanation_sections.lesson: When first differences are multiples of a number, compute second differences before assuming a GP; a constant second-difference means a quadratic sequence, not geometric.
explanation_sections.timing: 55 seconds. Two rounds of differencing needed plus one arithmetic step. Trap: reading 3,6,12 as a GP with ratio 2 and projecting 24 as the next first-difference (gives 71), or stopping after noticing multiples of 3 without the second-difference check.
